episode_title: Building the Okanagan: Construction Contracts, Liens, and Prompt Payment Explained

real_qa.q: What percentage of residential home construction costs in Canada comes from government fees, charges, and taxes?
real_qa.r: According to Cassidy DeVere, 30% of the cost of a home is government fees, charges and taxes on average across Canada. He emphasized that housing is taxed like cigarettes and alcohol, which represents a massive part of the overall construction cost problem.
real_qa.requete: government fees taxes percentage home construction cost Canada

real_qa.q: How many companies typically work on an average residential construction project?
real_qa.r: On average, any construction project will have 63 different companies working on it, according to Cassidy DeVere. This is why strong networking and relationship building are pivotal in the construction industry.
real_qa.requete: how many companies work construction project

real_qa.q: What is prompt payment legislation and how does it differ from the current Builders Lien Act in British Columbia?
real_qa.r: Prompt payment legislation sets out certain timelines that payments must be made by or disputes must be raised, with a third-party arbiter (free or cheap) to keep projects moving rather than having a complete breakdown with liens being filed. It codifies what already exists in the commercial world with payment certifiers, but the residential world currently lacks this structure. The 28-day payment timeline was selected based on the UK model, though it doesn't align with mortgage draw schedules.
real_qa.requete: prompt payment legislation British Columbia residential construction

real_qa.q: What percentage of Canadians under age 45 want to own a home according to Abacus Data research cited by the Canadian Home Builders Association?
real_qa.r: The national office of the Canadian Home Builders Association commissioned Abacus Data to conduct polling, which showed that in the high 80s of people under the age of 45 still wanted to own a home. However, the number of them that believed homeownership was realistic was pretty low.
real_qa.requete: Abacus Data homeownership Canadians under 45 percentage

real_qa.q: What is the current lien period timeframe under the Builders Lien Act in British Columbia, and what extension was recommended?
real_qa.r: The current lean period is 45 days, which Cassidy DeVere stated is not long enough time, particularly when invoicing monthly and waiting on mortgage draws. The recommendation from the BC Law Society was to extend this to 60 days to provide adequate time for the payment process.
real_qa.requete: Builders Lien Act 45 days period British Columbia

guest.entreprise: Canadian Home Builders Association in Central Okanagan
guest.bio_context: Cassidy DeVere comes from a multi-generational building family; his parents and grandparents were builders, and he ran his own construction company before joining the Canadian Home Builders Association. He represents residential builders across the Central Okanagan region, from Peachland to Enderby, focusing on education, advocacy, and networking for the home building industry.
